- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially in early horizon.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.5), model often underestimates; adjust upward, particularly if recent price action shows resilience.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days), model frequently overshoots in next 5-10 days; apply downward correction to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; check for mean reversion in 7-14 day window and reduce forecast slope.
- Model tends to overpredict in 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile (±0.5+); apply smoothing or reduce forecast amplitude by 5-10%.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +1 → -1 → +1), model often misreads momentum; use sentiment lag (e.g., 3-day sentiment) to adjust forecast direction.
- In low-sentiment periods (sentiment < 0.1), model often underperforms; increase forecast by 3-5% to account for hidden market resilience.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.0–0.3), model often fails to capture mean reversion; use 14-day moving average of true prices as baseline for correction.
